authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't add theft cards just for popularity (blueprint L51).
Don't over-invest in damage-only evasion (blueprint L52).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Nathan is a small attacker; blockers and removal shut off the engine.
No deterministic win, so long games against interaction-heavy tables.
Stolen spells need mana during combat.

value.interaction: Mana Drain, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Blasphemous Act.
value.mana: 34 lands, Sol Ring, Lotus Petal, Dark Ritual, Talismans.
value.protection: Boots, Greaves, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Nathan is the main card-advantage engine and the reason the list values trigger copies and combat-time mana.
accepted_role.honest_note: Commander Spellbook finds no combos in the list, and the source says the deck doesn't run a generic Oracle/Breach finish (blueprint L41). It wins by accumulated advantage and combat damage, so it's a low-to-mid Bracket 4 value deck. Nathan is central to the engine but provides no compact kill. The cycle 51 M1 review (nathan-01..08) verifies the engine and flags one anti-synergy (nathan-07).
